coverage.main: Read all thirteen pages of arXiv 1905.00441v3 (9 December 2019; ICML 2019): Sections 1-5, Algorithm 1, Table 1, Figures 1-2, references and supplementary pages 12-13 (defense descriptions, regression network, run-time Table 2). Figure 2 values read from a 200-dpi render of p. 8.
coverage.supplement: Supplementary material is appended in the arXiv PDF (pp. 12-13) and read. The PMLR version was not retrieved.
coverage.excluded_results: Table 1 and Figure 1 report query-based or white-box attacks on each target defense itself; supplement Table 2 is run time. The 100.00 diagonal of Figure 2 is the source itself.

result_groups.population: For each CIFAR-10 source DNN, 1,000 random test images that the source classifies correctly and whose adversarial versions the source misclassifies; transferred to the other defended/vanilla DNNs (8 models for BPDA, 10 for NATTACK)
result_groups.outcome: attack success rate on the target DNN, printed to two decimals
result_groups.evidence: Section 3.3: 'we randomly select 1000 images for each targeted DNN such that they are classified correctly, and yet the adversarial images of them are classified incorrectly', an explicit source-clean-correct and source-success restriction; the 100.00 diagonal is consistent. Target clean correctness is not stated, and source-only filtering does not establish it.

f1.evidence: Clean accuracy is reported separately for every model in Figure 2: ADV-TRAIN 87.3, ADV-BNN 79.7, THERM-ADV 88.5, CAS-ADV 75.6, LID 66.9, THERM 92.8, SAP 93.3, RSE 91.4 (Table 1) and VANILLA-1 80%, VANILLA-2 92.3% (Section 3.3). These are test-set accuracies, not accuracies on the transfer subsets.

f2.evidence: Only source correctness is stated. The two-decimal Figure 2 values are not multiples of 0.1% (e.g., 33.58%), so the effective denominator is not the stated 1,000 images; it might reflect a target-side filter, but this is not reported and is not inferred.

f3.evidence: Only adversarial images that fool the source are transferred. Positive conditioning evidence.

f4.evidence: The stated 1,000-image set cannot produce most printed two-decimal rates, so numerators cannot be reconstructed and the actual denominators are unreported.

f5.evidence: L-infinity threshold in normalized [0,1] space; the transfer study sets tau_inf = 0.031 for all models, including CAS-ADV changed from 0.015 'for fair comparison'.

f6.evidence: The linked repository contains the NATTACK attack, per-defense wrappers borrowed from Athalye et al., and a SharePoint link for data and models. Its confusion.py only plots hard-coded percentages (and stores the NATTACK matrix transposed relative to the published figure for the shared models); no transfer-evaluation script or per-example outcomes are included. SharePoint contents not accessed.

artifact_checks.result: Listed the tree via the GitHub API (head 9 February 2021): attack and defense wrappers (cascade_adv_training, guided-denoiser, inputtransformations, etc.) and confusion.py. README points to a UCF SharePoint folder for data and models. Not cloned or executed.

bounds_checks.reason: Rates are conditioned on source correctness and source success, with unreported target denominators; several targets (SAP, RSE, ADV-BNN ensemble) are stochastic. Not an unconditional misclassification rate; no bound.

limitations: Non-blind evidence audit. The row/column orientation of Figure 2 (caption: rows are sources) conflicts with the released plotting script's matrix orientation; flagged, not resolved.
